newsitem.title: ANGOLA: U.N. says its envoy to talk to Mandela over Angola.
newsitem.headline: U.N. says its envoy to talk to Mandela over Angola.

text.p: The U.N. special representative to Angola, Alioune Blondin Beye, left Luanda on Thursday to meet South African President Nelson Mandela, a spokesman said.
David Wimhurst, spokesman for the U.N. Angola Verification Mission monitoring implemention of a 1994 peace accord that ended nearly two decades of civil war, confirmed Beye had left at 0500 GMT.
Beye's trip to South Africa was one of several meetings aimed at ensuring there were no disruptions to the timetable set for the establishment of Angola's new unity government, he said.

Beye met former rebel UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi at his Bailundo headquarters in central Angola on Monday, and on Wednesday held talks with Angolan President Jose Eduardo dos Santos and Prime Minister Fernando Franca Van Dunem.
"He (Beye) is involved in a series of very intense consultations with all the key players. This visit to South Africa follows on these consultations," Wimhurst told Reuters.

"President Mandela is probably one of the most widely respected figures in the world," he said. "He's a man of influence and that's why he's got involved, but he has made it very clear South Africa does not intend to take on a mediation role."
Savimbi came to South Africa to see Mandela earlier this month.

South African officials were unavailable for comment on Thursday, while Mandela was locked in talks at a secret bush hideaway with colleagues from his African National Congress planning government and party policy for the next two years.
Angola's MPLA-led government and UNITA are trying to form a government of national reconciliation under the peace plan, but progress has been slow.
UNITA has proposed that Savimbi head the official opposition in parliament, rather than be a vice-president under dos Santos as the president had offered.
The new government is due to be inaugurated on January 25.
